newsitem.title: USA: ITT bidding for SEAT SpA, Italian 'Yellow Pages' publisher.
newsitem.headline: ITT bidding for SEAT SpA, Italian 'Yellow Pages' publisher.

text.p: ITT Corp., the target of a $6.5 billion hostile takeover bid from rival Hilton Hotels Corp., said Friday it was seeking, along with other partners, to acquire SEAT SpA, a telephone directory publisher in Italy.

"It is an extremely valuable piece of property. We would have been derelict in our duties had we not bid on SEAT," spokesman Jim Gallagher said when asked about ITT's plans regarding the Italian "Yellow Pages" publisher.

"Our plan was that our bid would be part of a consortium. We never had the intention of footing the bill alone. We have some partners in mind," Gallagher added, although he declined to identify any potential partners.
Gallagher confirmed reports that SEAT's value was near $1.6 billion but said ITT would spend no more than one-tenth of the value of the business over several years.
He refused to say what ITT's plans were for SEAT in the future.
There has been speculation that ITT would sell its World Directories unit as part of its plan to shed non-core assets to fend off Hilton's hostile bid, made earlier this month.

While Gallagher said the SEAT acquisition would be "significantly accretive" to ITT, he also admitted that SEAT would make "ITT directories significantly more valuable whether we plan to own it or someone else owns it."
When ITT rejected Hilton's unsolicited offer last week, it said it planned to focus on its core business of casinos and hotels. The SEAT SpA bid does not depart from that plan, Gallagher said.
"It in no way signals a change in our very specific direction that we announced in rejecting the Hilton offer," Gallagher said.
